title: Break The Spin · Nov 26-C (Harwich Elementary holiday memo)
subtitle: 1 post, real photo (National Christmas Tree). Scott approved as-is.

posts.theme: Massachusetts principal tells staff to keep the school holiday-free in December
posts.quote: Massachusetts Principal Bans Christmas Trees And Santa From Her School.
posts.alt: Photo of the lit National Christmas Tree on the Ellipse at night, with a star on top. Headline text: Massachusetts Principal Bans Christmas Trees And Santa From Her School. Break The Spin logo top left. Photo credit: National Park Service / Liz Macro.
posts.caption:
Principal Christie Cutone told staff at Harwich Elementary School in Massachusetts to keep the building a "holiday-free environment" this December.

The memo, sent Nov. 19, tells teachers to "refrain from putting up holiday-specific decorations (such as Christmas trees, wreaths, Elf on the Shelf, Santa imagery, menorahs, or dreidels)." Snowflakes, snowmen, and "cozy reading themes" are encouraged. Holiday worksheets, crafts, and videos are out too. If decorations go up, Cutone wrote, "we will gently ask that they be taken down."

Parents are pushing back. Abigail McGillen said her daughter already had a Halloween parade and a week of Thanksgiving activities. Inclusive, she told Boston 25, is "not to cancel traditions and cancel different cultures." "It's to celebrate them and teach these children."

Superintendent Robin Millen said "no policy changes have been made regarding holiday celebrations or recognitions in our schools." She called the memo a routine reminder. Parents say they have emailed administrators, and the guidance has not changed.

So Santa is a problem. A snowman is not.
posts.first:
The facts: Cutone is principal of Harwich Elementary, a pre-K through grade 4 school in the Monomoy Regional School District. The New England Signal obtained the Nov. 19 staff memo. The memo went to staff, not families, and does not use the phrase "safe space for every student." As of Nov. 26, it had not been publicly reversed.

Sources: Cape Cod Chronicle, Boston 25 News, The New England Signal, Newsweek.
